All 127 messages reference existing applications and users; every sender is permitted by rules sec.6 (recruiters, the job's hiring manager, or the application's own candidate); per-thread timestamps strictly increase (APP-101 has 120, matching app_context.md line 30). The 3 notes reference existing applications and are authored by a recruiter or the job's own manager (rules sec.3 Internal notes). All 6 read markers reference existing threads with 1<=read_count<=length; candidate markers belong to the application's candidate. Derived unread under rules sec.6 ('My own messages are never unread for me'): Lena on APP-301 = 1, matching the functional prompt Z claim 'the starting read markers give her 1'. stages, candidate_status_labels and thread_page_size 30 match rules sec.3/sec.7 tables and the 30-message page size; generated_note points to /instructions/hireops_rules.md, which exists. PII/secrets: all addresses use RFC 2606 reserved domains (hireops.example, candidates.example, mail.example); names are generic synthetic names; no DOB, phone, address, password, token or key in the seed; no non-ASCII. The demo password Hireops!2026 appears only in the public brief and in solution db.js line 63 (documented demo credential, the profile's expected case, not seed data). Injection: no '<', '>', URLs, template markers, 'ignore/system prompt' text or instructions in any free-text field; the only 'instruction' hit is the generated_note path. Colderwater lessons checked for this row: seed-quoted criterion figures (lesson 1/15) are publicly derivable from seed + rules; no public internet address in seed (lesson 13); restart check uses several seeded values (lesson 15). NOTE (P3, not a defect): two read markers sit below the reader's own later message: USR-CAN1 read_count 119 on APP-101 whose message #120 is USR-CAN1's own, and USR-REC3 read_count 2 on APP-301 whose message #3 is USR-REC3's own. Rules sec.6 say 'sending a message counts as reading the conversation', so this state could not arise from use. It has no grading consequence: the 'own messages are never unread' rule gives 0 unread for both regardless, seen status of the other party's last message is unaffected (REC1 marker 120 and REC3 marker 2 cover Noor's #120 and Lena's #2), and no criterion reads Noor's APP-101 or Farah's APP-301 starting unread count. Minor narrative oddity only: Farah's last message to Lena mentions 'once the panel has met' while Lena was rejected from Screen.
counterexample: Broken app that could pass this row's data-dependent checks: an app computing unread as total minus read_count still gives Lena 1 in Z, but hro_unread_counts also grades new-conversation legs, so seed data does not let it pass by itself. Conforming alternative that could fail: an app that normalises markers on load so senders have read their own messages (CAN1 to 120, REC3 to 3) gives identical unread and seen outcomes for every seeded value any prompt or criterion reads, so no conforming app is penalised. No failing counterexample found.
